Shower coverage has gradually increased with the approach of Invest
92W and is expected to become numerous tonight through tomorrow, with
wet conditions lasting longer for Guam and Rota. Isolated 
thunderstorms were observed today and are expected to continue
through Friday night. These thunderstorms and heavier showers could
have gusty winds through Friday. As discussed in the Tropical 
Systems section below, Invest 92W remains unlikely to pass through 
the Marianas as a tropical storm. However, the Marianas should still 
expect increasing showers, isolated thunderstorms, building seas and 
surf, and stronger winds. Afterwards, a ridge of high pressure will 
fill in once 92W passes, bringing drier conditions to the Marianas. 
Light winds could allow for island effect showers and thunderstorms 
in the afternoon periods Sunday and Monday. 

Marine...
Light to moderate east winds and combined seas of 3 to 5 ft are 
expected tonight for Guam and Rota. Seas are increasing slightly and
are expected to peak tonight or tomorrow at 4 to 6 ft with the 
passage of Invest 92W. Moderate east winds and combined seas of 5 to
6 feet are expected tonight through at least tomorrow morning for 
Tinian and Saipan as the northern trade wind amplified side of Invest
92W moves through. Isolated thunderstorms are possible through at
least Friday night. Gusty winds are possible with these 
thunderstorms tonight and into Friday. There will be a moderate risk
of rip currents along east facing reefs of the Marianas through at 
least Friday night.

Tropical Systems...
A weak disturbance, Invest 92W, is centered east-southeast of Guam 
near 11.7N 151.6E. Invest 92W is still rated medium, meaning 
development is expected, but not within the next 24 hours. 92W is 
moving west to west-northwest toward the Marianas. Invest 92W is 
expected to move through the Marianas within the next 24 hours, 
producing gusty winds and possible heavy rainfall across the islands 
as it moves through. 92W looks to strengthen after moving west of 
the Marianas.

For more information on Invest 92W, see bulletins issued by JTWC 
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Another weak disturbance, Invest 93W, is centered east-northeast of
Kosrae near 6N164E. Invest 93W lies along an active Near-Equatorial 
Trough (NET) that is producing numerous to widespread showers and 
isolated thunderstorms across a large portion of Micronesia. 93W 
looks to slowly move west to west-northwest over the next few days 
with little change in intensity expected. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The NET has become very active across eastern Micronesia. Numerous to
widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms are found over Kosrae
and just south of Pohnpei and Majuro. Invest 93W, centered east-
northeast of Kosrae, is helping to increase convergence over the 
area, resulting in increased convection. As Invest 93W drifts west 
to west-northwest, the NET looks to drift northward, pulling the 
numerous to widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms over 
Majuro and Pohnpei and maintaining the same over Kosrae, for the next
few days. Locally heavy rainfall is expected at least into the 
weekend and probably into the beginning of next week. Locally heavy 
showers will reduce visibilities across the islands and atolls, 
making driving hazardous through the weekend. Local flooding is 
possible for all three forecast points, with increased mudslide 
potential for Pohnpei and Kosrae, especially if the heavy rainfall 
continues into next week. majuro will see decreased convection first,
around Sunday, though POPs (Probability of Precipitation) look to 
slowly drop to 50 percent Sunday to around 30 percent Tuesday. Higher
POPs will continue at Kosrae until at least Monday and until Tuesday
for Pohnpei.

Other than thunderstorms heavy showers and possible gusty winds with
the convection, marine conditions will be fairly benign. Combined
seas will be at or below 5 feet through the week. Winds will be
mostly light to gentle, though strong gusts are possible with heavier
showers and thunderstorms.

Western Micronesia...
For Palau, Yap a gentle trade-wind pattern has set up over the 
western half of the region. A few weak trade-wind troughs are 
anticipated to bring a few light isolated showers over the next few 
days. Showers are anticipated to pick up over the weekend as the 
Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) is anticipated to reinvigorate bringing
showers back to the region.

For Chuuk, the NET, Invest 93W and accompanying showers/thunderstorms
are expected to move into the region tonight. Numerous to widespread
showers and isolated thunderstorms are to be expected over the next 
several days. Rainfall amounts of 5 to 10 inches through the weekend,
with locally heavier amounts possible. This will increase the threat
of flooding and mudslides for Weno. The NET is expected to remain 
active through the middle of next week, this could prolong the 
threats of flooding and mudslides.
